items.x_text:
Binance breach: about $6.3B in assets hit after a DevOps engineer's laptop led attackers to a service container that submitted unauthorized withdrawals. Binance: no private key leak. ~$3B frozen. TRM Labs and Chainalysis point to North Korea.

#DataBreach #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
$6.3 billion. It started with one engineer's laptop. 💸

What Binance disclosed (via The Hacker News, 30 Oct):
→ A 29 Oct "security incident" affected about $6.3B in assets; if confirmed, the largest crypto heist on record
→ Initial findings: a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop gave access to a service container that submitted unauthorized withdrawals
→ No evidence of a private key leak: Elliptic says the attacker got Binance's own systems to sign transactions
→ Nearly $3B has been frozen on-chain; Binance says it will cover all losses from SAFU and its own funds
→ TRM Labs and Chainalysis attribute it to North Korea with high confidence; Elliptic also links it to DPRK-linked actors but urges caution

Why it matters: you don't need to steal keys if you can reach the system that uses them. Lock down privileged engineer endpoints and require more than one approver for high-value transactions.

cover.hook: CVSS 10. No login. Now on CISA's exploited list.
cover.sub: GitLab CVE-2026-97229: a crafted regex in CI/CD config can run code on the server. Federal deadline: 1 Nov.

slides.title: What it is
slides.body: An integer overflow from weak regular expression validation in GitLab CE and EE. An unauthenticated user can send a crafted regex in a CI/CD configuration and execute code on the GitLab server.

slides.label: CVSS · added to CISA KEV on 29 Oct
slides.note: Federal agencies told to patch by 1 November 2026

slides.title: Who got hit
slides.body: Alpine Linux says an attacker sent crafted CI configs on 20-21 Oct, crashing GitLab workers 8 times. Alpine found no evidence it succeeded but couldn't rule it out, and rebuilt the instance from scratch.

slides.title: Fixed releases
slides.body: GitLab 19.2.8, 19.3.5 and 19.4.2 (critical patch release, 13 Oct). GitLab.com is already patched. Can't patch yet? Rapid7 suggests limiting anonymous access to public projects.

slides.title: What to do
items: Upgrade self-managed GitLab to a fixed release
Restrict anonymous access to public projects
Block untrusted users from writing to public projects
Check for repeated worker crashes since 20 Oct

items.x_text:
Claude Code extension 2.1.313 on the Cursor Marketplace was trojanized for about 11 hours on 29 Oct: it added an attacker SSH key, set persistence and sent host data out. Cursor says at most 5,000 users. Fixed in 2.1.314.

#SupplyChainAttack #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
The official Claude Code extension. Backdoored for about 11 hours. 🧩

What happened (via The Hacker News, 30 Oct):
→ Version 2.1.313 of anthropic.claude-code was pushed to the Cursor Marketplace under the legitimate publisher identity, live from about 2:27 a.m. to 1:35 p.m. PT on 29 Oct
→ A 66-line loader added an attacker SSH key ('svc-telemetry') to authorized_keys, tried to enable SSH and open a reverse tunnel, and set up persistence
→ It sent host details out: IP, hostname, username, Git email, and the names of secret-looking environment variables
→ Cursor says the version "was not developed by Anthropic" and at most 5,000 users were affected; no sign of it on Open VSX or Microsoft's marketplace
→ Found by OpenSourceMalware researchers; fixed version is 2.1.314

If you auto-updated that day: isolate the machine, remove the unknown SSH key and the scheduled task / crontab / LaunchAgent, and rotate credentials and sessions.

cover.sub: CrowdStrike says China-linked Vapor Panda ran ARTEX, an AI pentest framework, against ministries, telcos and defense firms.

slides.title: Who and when
slides.body: CrowdStrike attributes the activity to Vapor Panda, a China-based state-linked adversary. From 17 Oct it hit 200+ organisations: foreign ministries, telcos, and U.S. semiconductor, defense and think-tank targets.

slides.title: How the AI works
slides.body: ARTEX orchestrates several LLMs, here DeepSeek plus a commercial model. A planner agent directs worker agents through recon and lateral movement, trying paths in parallel and switching when one fails.

slides.title: What they used
slides.body: Old weaknesses, fast: auth keys unrotated since 2022 used to forge an admin token, cloud metadata reached via an XXE flaw, web shells, LAPS passwords read. Post-exploitation confirmed at 9 organisations.

Vapor Panda / ARTEX: CrowdStrike says the China-linked group used ARTEX, an AI pentest framework running DeepSeek and a commercial LLM, against 200+ organisations from 17 Oct. Planner and worker agents, a human steering.

#AISecurity #ThreatIntel
items.ig_caption:
200+ organisations. AI agents doing the legwork. A human steering. 🤖

What CrowdStrike found (via The Hacker News, 30 Oct):
→ China-based, state-linked Vapor Panda hit more than 200 organisations from 17 Oct: foreign ministries, telcos, U.S. semiconductor, defense and think-tank targets
→ It used ARTEX, a Go-based AI pentest framework that runs several LLMs; here DeepSeek and an unnamed commercial model
→ A planner agent directed worker agents from access to recon and lateral movement, trying paths in parallel; one intrusion used about 1.4 billion input tokens
→ The weaknesses were old: auth keys unrotated since 2022, cloud metadata reachable, web shells. Post-exploitation confirmed at 9 organisations

Why it matters: AI agents make a small team run many intrusions at once, and they're fast at finding the forgotten key. Rotate long-lived keys, lock down instance metadata access and hunt for web shells.

items.x_text:
WordPress core RCE (CVSS 8.1, versions 4.7 to 7.1.3): Wordfence blocked 62,969 attacks in 24 hours, racing to hit installer files staged during upgrades. Fixed in WordPress 7.1.4. Update, then check for new admin accounts.

#WordPress #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
62,969 attacks in 24 hours. On WordPress core itself. ⚠️

What Wordfence saw (via The Hacker News, 30 Oct):
→ A WordPress core remote code execution flaw, CVSS 8.1, affects versions 4.7 through 7.1.3 (no CVE yet)
→ During a full core upgrade, new files, including the installer, are unpacked into a predictable folder under wp-content/upgrade that's often web-reachable
→ An unauthenticated attacker has to hit that installer in a window of seconds, so attackers keep polling sites
→ Wordfence blocked 62,969 attacks in 24 hours; some sources polled the same sites for about 14.5 hours
→ Fixed in WordPress 7.1.4, released 28 Oct

What to do now: update to 7.1.4, look for requests to PHP files under wp-content/upgrade, and check for unfamiliar admin accounts, plugins or PHP files.
